note.p: MP for Beverley, friend of Tooke and member of the SCI, who chaired the fourteenth anniversary meeting of the SCI at the Crown and Anchor on 2 May 1794 - and was afterwards questioned about it by the Privy Council. Wharton may then have given evidence against Tooke - according to one account, Wharton relayed the information that Tooke had welcomed the prospect of a naval mutiny. 'The Privy Council could not decide whether to call Wharton as a prosecution witness or allow Tooke to call him for the defence, when the damnng evidence would be produced under cross-examination. They decided on the latter course when Tooke subpoenaed Wharton, but Tooke stymied the prosecution by not calling Wharton who was then unable to give evidence against him' (Gentleman Radical, p. 155).

He appears in the diary on 1 November 1794, when Godwin records seeing him at Hardy's trial. His name is crossed out under 1794 in the 1796 list and mistakenly entered under 1793 - he does not appear in this year. The two instances of 'Warton' in 1789 have been taken as unrelated - different spelling, context unconvincing, pre-date first appearance recorded in 1796 lists.

re 19.5.1793 Seward, Goring, Wathen at Tooke's: Although Wathen could have been Jonathan Wathen, noncomformist surgeon of Walbrook, or Josiah Iles Wathen, special pleader Middle Temple, Wharton came (inserted above the line) directly after Seward and Goring in 1793 in Godwin's 1796 list, so this was very likely John Wharton (History of Parliament) 1765-1843. Wharton also appeared twice in the 1796 list for 1794, both times crossed out, and neither time coded to John Wharton's person record in GD website. In the 1794 version of the 1796 list he appeared at the end of 1794. My suggestion is that Godwin compiled his lists by looking back through his diary, and his mis-spelling of the name first time confused him.
